fact_sheet.business_description: Nestlé S.A. operates as a global consumer packaged goods company selling products including coffee, infant nutrition, pet food, and bottled water [D01]. The company leverages global brands and local distribution, with coffee and pet-care franchises characterized by repeat purchases and brand investment [D01].
segments_and_separable_assets: L'Oréal stake (approximately 23% ownership, valued at >$25 billion) [D01, D04]
US confectionery business (annual sales of approximately $900 million) [D07]
economics_vs_peers: Management guidance indicates a roughly 300–400 basis-point margin gap versus selected peers [D06]
capital_structure: Parent book equity (FY2016): CHF 64,590 million [D02, D04]
management_board_governance: CEO: Mark Schneider, joined at the start of 2017 from Fresenius [D01, D07]
event_or_catalyst_evidence: Third Point advises selling the L'Oréal holding [D01, D03]
Company has indicated it may sell its US confectionery business [D07]
what_the_market_is_worried_about: Consumer shift toward fresher/local products and changing retail channels [D05]
Smaller competitors innovating faster than the global bureaucracy [D05]
Aggressive margin targets potentially damaging brands by shifting costs out of marketing [D05]
Tax implications and loss of compounding asset from selling the cosmetics stake [D05]
recent_events: 2017-06-25: Third Point discloses stake and strategy [D01, D07]
third_point_context: Third Point has taken a stake and advises selling the L'Oréal holding [D01, D03]

event_identified.evidence: Third Point identifies a 300-400 basis-point margin gap versus peers and advocates for the divestiture of the L'Oréal stake and US confectionery business [D01, D03, D06, D07].

edge.evidence: Third Point provides a specific plan to unlock value via margin improvement and portfolio simplification compared to the current operating model [D01, D06].

governance_route_or_process.evidence: As a large-cap company with a receptive register, the path involves private engagement and, if necessary, a public deck to press for capital allocation changes [D01, D07].

downside_floor.evidence: The company maintains a strong balance sheet with net debt of CHF 12.3 billion against CHF 64.6 billion in book equity and generates a 4.53% FCF yield [D02, D04].

size_and_liquidity.evidence: Given the market capitalization of CHF 255.5 billion, a multi-billion dollar position is achievable for Third Point [D04, D08].

management_credibility.evidence: New CEO Mark Schneider, having joined in 2017, provides a window to influence the strategic direction regarding margin targets and portfolio optimization [D01, D07].

gate1.edge_statement: Third Point identifies a structural margin gap and an opportunity to unlock value by monetizing non-core assets like the L'Oréal stake, providing a disciplined roadmap for a new CEO.
gate1.one_line_verdict: a conglomerate with a clear 300-400bps margin gap, separable high-value assets, and an opportunity for portfolio simplification under new management

gate2.variant_view: The market views Nestlé as a defensive, low-growth consumer staple hampered by a bloated conglomerate structure and aging assets, resulting in a persistent discount to higher-performing peers. Third Point believes that new management, under Mark Schneider, can drive a significant margin expansion of 300-400 basis points through aggressive portfolio pruning—specifically divesting the non-core L'Oréal stake and the struggling US confectionery unit—and by adopting a more disciplined capital allocation policy [D01, D06, D07]. This transformation will reveal the underlying value of its core coffee and pet-care franchises, which are currently obscured by corporate complexity [D01].
evidence: Management guidance acknowledges a 300-400 basis-point margin gap relative to peer benchmarks [D06].
Third Point explicitly advocates for the monetization of the ~23% L'Oréal stake, valued at over $25 billion [D01, D04].
The US confectionery business, with $900 million in sales, is identified as a prime candidate for divestiture [D07].
gate2.peer_benchmark: Selected high-performing consumer packaged goods peers with operating margins significantly above Nestlé's 15.3% reported 2016 level [D02, D06].
what_must_be_true: New CEO Mark Schneider remains committed to a mandate of portfolio optimization and operational efficiency.
The Board supports the divestiture of the L'Oréal stake despite tax or long-term compounding concerns.
Margin improvement initiatives do not inadvertently erode core brand equity through excessive cost-cutting.
The conglomerate discount narrows as the market gains confidence in the simplified business model.

arithmetic: Core business: 15.3% margin + 400bps improvement = 19.3% operating margin [D02, D06]
Peer average multiple applied to optimized FCF: ~25x [D04]
Target price represents a ~27% upside from CHF 82.65 [D04]

floor.basis: CHF 64.59 billion book equity plus resilient cash flows from coffee and pet-care franchises [D02, D04]

flagged_assumptions: Target multiple of 25x assumes market re-rating of core business following successful margin expansion and portfolio simplification
Tax leakage from potential L'Oreal disposal is not explicitly quantified in the pack

asks: Divest the ~23% L'Oréal stake to unlock capital for buybacks or core investment [D01, D04]
Divest the non-core US confectionery business [D07]
Implement a margin improvement plan to close the 300-400bps gap versus peers [D01, D06]
actors: Nestlé Board of Directors — Board — Target of engagement [D01]
gate4.governance_route: Private constructive engagement with new leadership to influence strategic direction and capital allocation [D01, D07]
gate4.escalation_path: If private dialogue fails to yield a concrete margin improvement plan or commitment to asset monetization within 2-3 quarters, transition to a public campaign including shareholder letters and presentations [D01].
gate4.why_this_role_fits_the_era: Fits the 2016+ strategy of private engagement first with mega-cap companies that have new leadership, reserving public confrontation for when initial strategic recommendations are ignored [D01, D07].

kill_criteria: Mark Schneider rejects the necessity of a margin improvement plan or confirms a permanent retention of the L'Oréal stake [D01].
Company reports two consecutive quarters of margin contraction instead of the planned expansion [D06].
Structural shift in the coffee or pet-care markets impairs the core franchise profitability [D01].
Increased regulatory or tax-related hurdles render the divestiture of the US confectionery unit or L'Oréal stake value-destructive [D07].
gate5.portfolio_risk: Factor overlap exists with other global mega-cap consumer staples; as a large-cap position, liquidity is sufficient for entry and exit, though we must manage gross exposure in the context of a $16B AUM fund [D04, D08].
gate5.hedge_overlay: Index puts or consumer sector-specific short baskets to mitigate market beta risk while pursuing idiosyncratic margin-expansion catalysts.
gate5.biggest_risk_in_one_sentence: Execution risk regarding margin improvement and the board's reluctance to monetize the L'Oréal stake could lead to a prolonged period of stagnant performance despite a compelling valuation floor.

asks: Divest the non-core US confectionery business
Implement a margin improvement plan to close the 300-400bps gap versus peers

drivers.driver: Nestlé is a world-class consumer conglomerate trading at a discount because of a persistent 300-400bps margin gap versus its peers [D01, D06].
The company holds a non-core ~23% stake in L'Oréal valued at over $25 billion, which should be monetized to unlock capital [D01, D04].
New CEO Mark Schneider represents an inflection point for the organization to adopt a more disciplined capital allocation and operational strategy [D01, D07].
The US confectionery business, with $900 million in annual sales, is an identified candidate for divestiture to further simplify the portfolio [D07].

kill_criteria: Mark Schneider rejects the necessity of a margin improvement plan.
Company confirms permanent retention of the L'Oréal stake.
Two consecutive quarters of margin contraction.
Structural impairment of the core coffee or pet-care franchises.
final.what_would_change_our_mind: A definitive rejection of portfolio simplification by the Board or a breakdown in the core growth franchises which would erode the long-term margin target potential.
final.memo:
Nestlé is a global powerhouse in coffee, infant nutrition, and pet care, yet its performance is obscured by a bloat-prone conglomerate structure that leaves a 300-400 basis-point operating margin gap against its peers [D01, D06]. At a trailing P/E of 30.1x, the market is failing to credit the company for its potential for operational excellence [D04].

By applying a 19.3% operating margin to the core business and factoring in the monetization of the ~23% L'Oréal stake—worth over $25 billion—we see a clear path to a valuation of CHF 105.00 per share [D01, D02, D04, D06]. This represents a compelling ~27% upside from the recent price of CHF 82.65 [D04].

With new CEO Mark Schneider at the helm, the company has a unique window to transition toward a leaner model [D01, D07]. Our plan is straightforward: we are pushing for the divestiture of the L'Oréal holding and the non-core US confectionery business to catalyze a rerating of the core assets [D01, D07].

We engage privately as constructive partners, though we are prepared to escalate if progress on margin targets or asset monetization is not observed within 2-3 quarters [D01]. We view the CHF 75.00 level as a hard floor supported by the strength of the underlying coffee and pet-care franchises [D02, D04]. We are initiating a position at 5% of NAV, with a target of 8% as our engagement progresses [D05].
